Threat actors distributing the ShadowLynx loader have been observed staging
payloads on compromised WordPress sites over the past two weeks.

Initial access is achieved via a phishing email sent from
finance-support[@]corp-billing[.]com containing a link to
hxxps://cdn-updates[.]net/invoice/setup.exe.

Once executed, the loader (SHA256:
9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08) drops a
second-stage payload identified by its MD5 hash
d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e and reaches out to command-and-control
infrastructure at 185.220.101.45 and c2.shadowlynx-panel[.]ru.

Persistence is established via the registry key
HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Updater.

A Bitcoin wallet associated with the ransom note was identified as
1BoatSLRHtKNngkdXEeobR76b53LETtpyT.

The sample was also seen communicating over
hxxp://185.220.101.45:8080/gate.php.
